content: Kinfo (broker-synced trading analytics with a community leaderboard) is the direct precedent for shared social stats in a trading journal: users choose a sharing tier (nothing / percentages only / percentages+dollars), account size is never shown regardless of tier, and a nickname (not real name) is the public identity, with an opt-out. Even so, community discussion frames Kinfo's social layer as creating as many problems as it solves. This is in tension with the project's envelope-encryption/no-cross-user-read posture — any shared surface requires a deliberate, separate, explicitly-opted-in read path, not a relaxation of the default isolation. Source: JournalPlus and trading-journals.com reviews of Kinfo (secondary reviews, MEDIUM).
